prompt: Nowadays, young people communicate with friends and family through mostly social network sites, rather than other ways of communication like talking on the phone or face to face. Do you think it is a positive or negative
essay:
Nowadays, many young people communicate with their friends and family mainly through social networking sites instead of talking on the phone or meeting face to face. I believe this is a negative development because it can reduce real relationships and cause communication problems.

On the one hand, social networking sites have some advantages. Firstly, they make communication quick and easy. Young people can send messages, photos and videos to their friends and family at any time. Secondly, these websites are useful when people live far away from each other. For example, a young person who studies in another country can easily stay in contact with his or her parents through social media. Therefore, social networking can help people maintain relationships over long distances.

On the other hand, there are several disadvantages. The main problem is that young people may spend too much time online and have less face-to-face communication. As a result, they may become less confident when speaking with people in real life. In addition, messages on social media can sometimes be misunderstood because people cannot see the other person’s facial expressions or body language. Spending too much time on social networking can also reduce family time. For example, some young people use their phones during meals instead of talking with their family members.

In my opinion, social networking is useful, but it should not replace traditional communication completely. Young people should use social media to stay connected, but they should also talk on the phone and meet their friends and family in person. This can help them develop stronger relationships and better communication skills.

In conclusion, although social networking has made communication easier, I believe depending on it too much is a negative development.
